source_snapshot.procedure: Run in-band raw DCMI 0x2c/0x10 with request `dc 01 <Entity ID> 01 00` for listed entities 0x40 inlet, 0x41 CPU and 0x42 baseboard, then check the response.
source_snapshot.criteria: Command should be sent without any error.
source_snapshot.deepseek_finding: DeepSeek changes the source raw command to an SSH-wrapped high-level command with operator variables and an example 0x44 entity not present in this row; its output instruction leaves all interpretation to the user.

original_test_intent.purpose: Verify through the host in-band IPMI path that the BMC accepts DCMI Get Temperature Readings for source-listed inlet, CPU and baseboard entity IDs and returns structurally valid temperature data for entity instance 01h.
original_test_intent.target: The selected SUT's local in-band BMC/IPMI interface and DCMI temperature entities 40h, 41h and 42h, each queried for entity instance 01h as written in the workbook.
original_test_intent.scope: Issue one raw request per listed entity, require successful completion and a valid DCMI response containing the DCh group identifier, available-instance count, returned-set count and signed Celsius/instance pair. This source command does not enumerate every CPU/core or every entity instance.
original_test_intent.operation: Verify SUT and local IPMI access, preserve existing logs, send raw 2Ch/10h with `dc 01 <entity> 01 00` for 40h, 41h and 42h, decode the exact response layout, retain unsupported/nonzero results and compare returned instance 01h with the requested entity context without issuing any thermal-control command.
original_test_intent.duration_and_iterations: The workbook estimates 10 attended and 5 machine minutes and prescribes one in-band request for each of three listed entity IDs.
original_test_intent.expected_result: Each supported entity request completes successfully, returns DCh, reports one returned temperature set for the nonzero instance request, and supplies a valid signed-Celsius byte followed by entity instance 01h. Platform-specific temperature reasonableness requires a contemporaneous sensor/reference policy and is not established by command success alone.
original_test_intent.required_evidence: SUT/BMC/firmware/local-interface/tool identity; timestamps; three exact raw requests; completion codes and complete response bytes; decoded total-instance count, returned-set count, signed Celsius value and instance number; unsupported records; and proof that no thermal, fan, power or log mutation occurred.
ambiguities: The source criterion requires only absence of a command error and supplies no expected temperature range or cross-sensor tolerance.
The CPU description refers to processor/core count, but the fixed request selects only entity instance 01h and therefore cannot prove coverage of all CPU temperature instances.
Entity Instance Start is 00h in the source although the standard says 01h starts enumeration; this byte is not used when Entity Instance is nonzero.
The source asks to clear logs even though the operation is read-only and log clearing is unrelated destructive activity.

v2_review_conclusion.finding: V2 correctly rejects DeepSeek's 0x44 example, keeps the three source entity IDs and removes log clearing. It incorrectly says the response contains entity echo, units/scaling, status and thresholds, none of which are fields in DCMI 1.5 Table 6-22, and it does not disclose that the source request selects only instance 01h rather than enumerating all instances.

applicable_history.decision: The historical review treated the case as executable and expected response collection; it did not establish platform-specific temperature limits or expand the source beyond the listed three entities.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: Keep the read-only FULLY AUTOMATABLE classification, but replace V2's nonexistent response fields with the exact DCMI 1.5 payload and state explicitly that the workbook command tests instance 01h only. Command conformance can be completed automatically; thermal reasonableness is a separate platform-specific judgment.

available_now: The source fixes the in-band path, net function, command, sensor type, three entity IDs and instance 01h.
DCMI 1.5 defines the exact request and response layout and the temperature encoding in Celsius.
The operation is read-only and can be bounded to three commands.
missing_inputs: Runtime target identity, authorized local privilege and qualified `ipmitool` are resolved from the lab assignment.
A platform sensor map and expected thermal range are needed only if the engineer wants to judge temperature plausibility beyond protocol success.
execution_readiness_detail.input_owner: The lab assignment supplies the SUT and local privilege; the platform/BMC owner supplies any product-specific sensor inventory, range or tolerance. These do not block the source-defined command-conformance collection.
safe_read_only_work_before_closure: Run the three fixed raw reads, decode every returned byte and preserve timestamped evidence.
prohibited_until_closed: Do not clear logs, set thermal limits, change fans or power, substitute entity 44h, claim all CPU/core sensors were covered, or declare platform thermal health without the applicable specification.
execution_readiness_detail.closure_verification: Confirm the exact SUT and local interface, obtain successful structurally valid responses for supported entities, preserve unsupported results without substitution, and separately identify any unresolved product-specific temperature judgment.

revision_candidate.test_name: In-Band DCMI Temperature Read for Listed Entity Instance 01h
revision_candidate.purpose: Verify that the local in-band IPMI path returns valid DCMI temperature data for instance 01h of the inlet, CPU and baseboard entity IDs listed by the source.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: An authorized server host with a working local IPMI interface and a BMC implementing DCMI Get Temperature Readings; product-specific sensor availability may differ.
revision_candidate.target_scope: Entity IDs 40h, 41h and 42h, entity instance 01h, one request each. Other entity IDs, additional instances and thermal-control behavior are outside scope.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Verified SUT/BMC/firmware identity; authorized local privilege; qualified `ipmitool`; DCMI 1.5 response decoder; optional platform sensor map/ranges for a separate plausibility judgment.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: Without clearing logs, execute `ipmitool raw 0x2c 0x10 0xdc 0x01 0x40 0x01 0x00`, then repeat with entity 41h and 42h. For each response, record completion and require DCh, total available instances, returned-set count 01h, a valid signed-Celsius byte and returned entity instance 01h. Record unsupported entities exactly; do not substitute another entity or infer unqueried-instance coverage.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Correct host and local BMC interface verified; no concurrent BMC reset; tool and decoder qualified; read-only authorization present; logs preserved.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Timestamped identity and tool version; the three redacted commands; complete raw responses and completion codes; decoded DCh, total-instance count, set count, signed Celsius and returned instance; any unsupported result; scope limitation and non-mutation audit.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: Intel Data Center Manageability Interface Specification v1.5 rev. 1.0, section 6.7.3 and Table 6-22, plus the platform sensor specification only for temperature plausibility.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Read only. Do not clear logs, set a thermal policy, alter fan/power state, expose credentials, silently change entity/instance, or represent a single instantaneous reading as a long-duration thermal test.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: None beyond normal authorization for the read-only local query. Engineer judgment is required only for product-specific thermal plausibility or whether unsupported entities violate the platform requirement.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: The agent can run and structurally validate the three reads. The engineer owns product-specific sensor presence, acceptable ranges and any decision to add all-instance enumeration as a separate scope.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: No state recovery is expected. On malformed output, preserve the exact bytes and stop decoding; on interface loss or BMC reset, stop and report rather than retrying without bounds.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Wrong target/interface; concurrent BMC reset; nonzero completion requiring diagnosis; missing DCh; truncated or inconsistent response; credential exposure; or any request to mutate thermal, fan, power or logs.

identified_defects: V2 invents entity echo, units/scaling, status and threshold response fields that Table 6-22 does not define.
V2 does not state that the source request selects only instance 01h and therefore cannot establish all CPU/core sensor coverage.
DeepSeek substitutes a non-source 44h example and an unsupported argument form for the high-level `get_temp_reading` command.
The source's log-clear step is unrelated destructive activity.
reason_for_change: Preserve the exact three-entity single-instance read while replacing V2's fabricated response semantics with the normative DCMI payload and preventing a single instance read from being overstated as complete CPU/core thermal coverage.

new_technical_evidence.title: Data Center Manageability Interface Specification
new_technical_evidence.supports: The request contains sensor type, entity ID, entity instance and instance start. A nonzero entity instance selects one instance; the response contains DCh, total instances, returned-set count and temperature/instance pairs, with signed Celsius encoding and a maximum of eight sets per response.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The standard does not define this product's required sensor population or acceptable operating range.

new_technical_evidence.title: ipmitool DCMI implementation
new_technical_evidence.applicability: Reference implementation of DCMI temperature enumeration
new_technical_evidence.supports: The implementation builds the five-byte DCMI request and enumerates 40h, 41h and 42h using entity instance 00h and a start offset, demonstrating that all-instance enumeration is distinct from the workbook's instance-01h request.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The DUT's installed ipmitool version and BMC behavior must be captured at runtime.

removed_ambiguities: Defines the actual response fields and signed-Celsius encoding.
States that the fixed source command covers instance 01h only.
Separates protocol conformance from platform temperature plausibility and long-duration thermal validation.
resolved_blockers: No blocker exists for bounded read-only protocol collection.
remaining_blockers: Product-specific PASS/FAIL for sensor presence or temperature range still needs the platform specification; it does not block raw collection.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 removes four nonexistent evidence fields, provides the exact normative response schema and prevents false all-instance coverage while retaining V2's correct safe automation classification.

agent_understanding_result.notes: Isolated validation confirmed exactly three DCMI temperature reads for entity IDs 40h, 41h and 42h at instance 01h, complete group/count/signed-Celsius/instance parsing, read-only boundaries, explicit unsupported disposition, and the limitation that protocol structure and units do not prove calibration, physical accuracy, thermal stability or PASS from one plausible value.

per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_purpose_fact: Functionality row 1284 fixes DCMI command 10h, sensor type 01h, entity IDs 40h/41h/42h and entity instance 01h over the local path.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_v2_comparison: V2 preserved entity IDs but invented response fields and did not disclose the single-instance boundary.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_safety_evidence_decision: Allow exactly three read-only local requests; prohibit log clearing, thermal controls, entity substitution and unqueried-instance claims.
